title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Carrying Out a Special Inspection of Commutation and Parole Work in All High and Intermediate People's Courts Nationwide
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Conducting a Special Inspection of Commutation and Parole Work in All High and Intermediate People's Courts Nationwide

Fa [2004] No. 121

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

To further implement the working theme of "justice and efficiency" of the people's courts, uphold judicial justice, and ensure the correct execution of criminal punishments, the Supreme People's Court has decided to conduct a special inspection of commutation and parole work in all High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts nationwide. The arrangements and requirements for this inspection are hereby notified as follows:

I. Purpose and Significance of the Inspection

Commutation and parole are important systems for the execution of criminal punishments stipulated in the Criminal Law and the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and are important components of the criminal trial work of the people's courts. Commutation and parole work concerns the execution of punishments and the rehabilitation of offenders, relates to the maintenance of supervision order in correctional facilities, and affects the vital interests of persons serving sentences. Over the years, all High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts nationwide, despite having few judicial personnel and heavy trial tasks, have handled a large number of commutation and parole cases in strict accordance with the Criminal Law, the Criminal Procedure Law, and judicial interpretations, playing an active role in rehabilitating offenders, preventing crimes, and maintaining social stability. At the same time, we should be clearly aware that there are still some problems in the commutation and parole work of courts nationwide that cannot be ignored. If these problems are not taken seriously and resolved, commutation and parole work will be affected, punishments cannot be correctly executed, and judicial justice and the authority of the law will not be guaranteed. To this end, the Supreme People's Court has decided to conduct a special inspection of commutation and parole work nationwide from June of this year to March of next year. The purpose is to summarize work experience, conscientiously clean up and correct existing problems, and further improve and strengthen commutation and parole work.

II. Scope and Content of Cases Subject to Inspection

The scope of the special inspection of commutation and parole work covers commutation and parole cases handled by all High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts since 1998, with a focus on cases since 2001. The main contents of the inspection are as follows:

(A) Basic Information on Commutation and Parole Cases Handled by People's Courts

1. The number of persons for whom the penal enforcement authorities requested the people's court to grant commutation or parole each year (excluding commutation from death sentence with a two-year reprieve), the number of persons for whom the people's court ruled to grant, modify, or deny commutation or parole, and the reasons for modifying or denying commutation or parole;

2. The number of persons serving sentences originally sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve for whom the penal enforcement authorities requested commutation each year, the number of persons for whom the people's court ruled to commute to life imprisonment or fixed-term imprisonment, and the reasons for commuting to fixed-term imprisonment.

(B) Basic Practices of People's Courts in Adjudicating Commutation and Parole Cases

1. The methods used by people's courts to adjudicate commutation and parole cases, including the respective numbers of cases handled by documentary review, court hearings, public hearings, and public notice;

2. What other measures have been taken to ensure the quality and efficiency of handling commutation and parole cases.

(C) Problems Existing in Commutation and Parole Work

1. What problems exist in the implementation of laws and judicial interpretations, and whether there are cases of handling cases in violation of law;

2. What problems exist in the quality and efficiency of case handling;

3. Whether there are phenomena of handling "connection cases," "favor cases," or "money cases" in violation of law or discipline, whether there are cases where judicial personnel accept bribes, engage in malpractice for personal gain, or commit perversion of justice, or cases of unjust adjudication that have aroused strong public reaction, and how the responsible persons have been dealt with.

(D) Handling of Cases Where the Procuratorial Authority Has Submitted Written Opinions of Correction

1. The number and reasons for cases in which the procuratorial authority has submitted opinions of correction;

2. The number of cases in which the people's court has made corrections and those in which corrections have not been adopted, and the reasons for not making corrections.

III. Methods and Steps of the Inspection

The special inspection of commutation and parole work shall be conducted primarily through self-inspection by each High People's Court and Intermediate People's Court, supplemented by random inspections by higher-level people's courts.

The inspection is divided into four stages: The first stage, from June to early July, is the mobilization, study, and deployment stage. During this stage, relevant laws and judicial interpretations shall be organized for study, ideological mobilization shall be carried out to make judicial personnel fully aware of the significance of this inspection, clarify the purpose and requirements of the inspection, and, in light of the actual conditions of their own units, study, formulate, and deploy inspection work plans and measures. The second stage, from early July to the end of September, is the self-inspection stage. Each High People's Court and Intermediate People's Court shall, based on the scope, content, and requirements of the inspection, conduct a serious inspection of the commutation and parole cases handled by its own court. The third stage, from October to the end of November, is the random inspection stage. Each High People's Court shall conduct random inspections of the commutation and parole work and the progress of the inspection carried out by the Intermediate People's Courts under its jurisdiction. The fourth stage, from December to March of next year, is the rectification stage. Each High People's Court and Intermediate People's Court shall, in response to the problems identified, analyze the causes, identify gaps, summarize experience, improve systems, and establish and perfect operating procedures for handling commutation and parole cases.

IV. Work Requirements for the Inspection

Conducting this inspection is of great significance for consolidating the achievements of the judicial inspection, establishing an image of impartial justice for the people's courts, strengthening the building of court personnel, and strengthening and improving criminal trial work. To ensure the smooth progress of the inspection and to achieve tangible results and the desired objectives, the following work requirements are put forward:

1. To enable higher-level people's courts to timely and accurately understand and grasp the progress of inspections in various localities, a reporting system for inspection work shall be established. Starting from June 30, 2004, each High People's Court and Intermediate People's Court shall report the progress of the inspection every half month, including information on deployment, measures, progress, existing problems, and relevant suggestions. Among them, each High People's Court shall report to the Supreme People's Court on the 15th and 30th of each month. After the end of each stage of the inspection, a stage work report shall be submitted; after the conclusion of the inspection activity, a comprehensive summary report shall be prepared and submitted separately.

2. In conducting the special inspection of commutation and parole work, achievements and experiences, especially explorations and successful experiences in reforming and improving the commutation and parole system, shall be conscientiously summarized. At the same time, problems existing in the work shall be seriously examined, the causes of problems shall be analyzed, the nature and responsibilities shall be distinguished, and cases shall be dealt with separately. Among them, for cases of improper commutation or parole discovered during the inspection, if correction is possible within the statutory time limit, they shall be resolutely and promptly corrected according to law; for cases that have exceeded the statutory time limit and are not suitable for modification, the reasons shall be explained and lessons shall be drawn; for problems discovered that involve relevant departments, communication shall be made with those departments in a timely manner; for persons and matters found to be in violation of law or discipline, they shall be seriously dealt with strictly in accordance with trial discipline and relevant laws; for problems and loopholes exposed in the work, targeted rectification measures shall be formulated, and strict work systems shall be established. In the future, to ensure the transparency and fairness of commutation and parole cases, a public notice system and a conditional public hearing system shall be implemented for all commutation and parole cases.

3. Each High People's Court and Intermediate People's Court shall effectively strengthen the organization and leadership of the inspection work. The principal leader shall personally take charge, and the deputy president in charge shall serve as the first person responsible for this special inspection, specifically responsible for leading this work. Courts in various localities shall, in accordance with the unified deployment and requirements of the Supreme People's Court and in light of their actual local conditions, conscientiously study and formulate feasible work plans to ensure that the inspection is carried out effectively. The Supreme People's Court shall send several inspection teams at appropriate times to various localities in batches for work inspections.

4. In conducting the inspection, opinions from local Party committees and people's congresses shall be earnestly solicited. Attention shall be paid to maintaining close contact with the procuratorial authorities, prison administration authorities, and public security detention centers, proactively understanding the situation and communicating information. For problems discovered during the law enforcement inspection of prisons and detention centers conducted by the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice, any matters involving the work of the people's courts themselves shall be promptly verified. Opinions and suggestions from relevant parties shall be taken seriously, studied promptly, and resolved earnestly. At the same time, such information shall be promptly reported to higher-level courts.

5. Publicity and reporting of the inspection shall be carried out well. This special inspection of commutation and parole work in the national court system is of great significance and has drawn considerable social attention. Therefore, courts in various localities shall pay attention to the publicity and reporting of the inspection, integrate this activity with the ongoing "Establishing an Image through Judicial Justice" education campaign, and through news media and various means, objectively publicize the achievements and experiences of the people's courts in commutation and parole work, establish a positive image of the people's courts strictly handling commutation and parole cases according to law and upholding judicial justice, and strive for societal understanding, concern, and support for the commutation and parole work of the people's courts, thereby creating a favorable judicial environment and public opinion atmosphere.

June 24, 2004
